# Shortcut test: labels predicted from file properties only (generated by `python -m brainguard.shortcut`)

Model: gradient boosting on width, height, aspect ratio, colour mode, file size and bytes per pixel. No pixel values. Trained on Kaggle Training, scored on Kaggle Testing (1,311 images).

| Task | Result on Testing |
|---|---|
| Tumour vs no tumour | **AUC 0.984** (95% CI 0.978–0.990) · accuracy 94.0% (92.6%–95.1%) · balanced accuracy 95.4% |
| One rule: "not 512×512 → no tumour" | accuracy 90.5% (88.8%–91.9%) |
| 4 classes | accuracy 67.1% (64.5%–69.6%) · balanced accuracy 64.5% · majority-class baseline 30.9% |

Interpretation: the no-tumour class comes from a different source than the tumour classes, so image geometry and encoding alone separate them. An image model's accuracy on this dataset cannot be read as evidence that it recognises tumours.
